To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the substructure accuracy is best when F(A) values are truncated to 3.0 A resolution and that the accuracy of the substructures obtained from anomalous differences decreases with the resolution at which the differences are truncated.

the accuracy and precision of selenium substructures are improved by: (i) using F(+) values instead of F(A) values, (ii) using anomalous differences truncated below 2.5 angstrom, (iii) using the full resolution range of the data and (iv) applying the substructure determination program SHELXD to a single data set instead of to several data sets.

the use of F(A) values is superior to the use of anomalous differences for the determination of selenium substructures, that the resolution limit of the substructure determination should be set at 2.5 A, and that the use of the F(A) values should be restricted to the highest resolution shells.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, if possible, the highest-resolution data should be used to determine the substructure.
a substructure determination based on F(A) or anomalous differences truncated at 3 sigma is not recommended.
, for a given data set, a substructure model obtained from a subset of the data is as good as a model obtained from all data, provided the data subset is chosen appropriately.
